questions.question_text: A sponge maintains a water current through its body while collar cells trap suspended food. Which cells perform this role?
questions.explanation: Choanocytes (collar cells) generate water flow and capture food particles in sponges.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Water enters a sponge through many small pores and leaves through a larger opening. What is the larger exit opening called?
questions.explanation: Water exits a sponge through the osculum after passing through its canal system and central cavity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A freshwater Hydra traps prey with tentacles, then digests it in a central cavity with a single opening. Which structural plan does this illustrate?
questions.option_b: Complete digestive tract with separate mouth and anus
questions.explanation: Cnidarians such as Hydra have a gastrovascular cavity with one opening that serves as both mouth and exit for undigested material.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A small freshwater cnidarian develops a genetically similar outgrowth that detaches as a new individual. Which reproductive process is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Hydra commonly reproduces asexually by budding; the outgrowth develops and separates from the parent.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A flatworm has flame-shaped excretory cells connected to tubules. Which structure is being described?
questions.explanation: Many flatworms use protonephridia with flame cells for osmoregulation and waste removal.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A tapeworm lives in the intestine of a host and absorbs digested nutrients across its body surface. Which feature supports this mode of life?
questions.option_c: A highly reduced or absent digestive tract
questions.option_d: A complete digestive tract with a large stomach
questions.explanation: Tapeworms absorb nutrients through their tegument and have a reduced digestive system because they live in a nutrient-rich host gut.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A roundworm has a fluid-filled body cavity that is not completely lined by mesoderm. This cavity is a:
questions.explanation: Nematodes are pseudocoelomates: their body cavity is not fully lined by mesoderm.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A preserved roundworm specimen has separate male and female individuals, unlike the usual earthworm condition. Which group best fits?
questions.explanation: Many nematodes, including Ascaris, have separate sexes; earthworms are generally hermaphroditic.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An earthworm’s blood remains within vessels as it circulates. Which type of circulatory system does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Earthworms have a closed circulatory system in which blood flows through vessels.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A leech attaches to a host using anterior and posterior suckers. The suckers are primarily adaptations for:
questions.explanation: Leeches use suckers to attach to hosts or substrates and aid movement.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An insect continues gas exchange even when oxygen delivery does not depend primarily on blood haemoglobin. Which structure transports air through branching tubes to tissues?
questions.explanation: Insects use a tracheal system: air travels through tracheae and finer tracheoles toward tissues.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A terrestrial arthropod has book lungs and four pairs of walking legs. Which group is most consistent with these traits?
questions.explanation: Many arachnids such as spiders have book lungs and four pairs of walking legs, unlike insects with three pairs.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A crab exchanges gases using gills and has two pairs of antennae. Which arthropod group does it belong to?
questions.explanation: Crustaceans commonly have gills and two pairs of antennae.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A mollusc scrapes algae from a surface with a ribbon-like feeding organ bearing rows of tiny teeth. This organ is the:
questions.explanation: The radula is a rasping feeding organ in most molluscs; bivalves are a notable exception.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a clam, which tissue layer commonly secretes the shell?
questions.explanation: The mantle of a mollusc secretes the shell and encloses the mantle cavity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which trait distinguishes cephalopods such as octopuses from most other molluscs in circulation?
questions.option_a: They possess a water vascular system
questions.option_b: They have a closed circulatory system
questions.option_d: They are all sessile filter feeders
questions.explanation: Cephalopods have a closed circulatory system, an exception among molluscs which generally have open circulation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sea urchin has small hard plates embedded beneath its skin. What material chiefly forms these internal skeletal ossicles?
questions.explanation: Echinoderms possess a calcareous internal endoskeleton made of ossicles, commonly composed of calcium carbonate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which observation is characteristic of echinoderm development rather than their adult body plan?
questions.option_a: Adults have jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeletons
questions.option_b: Larvae have a notochord that persists throughout life
questions.option_c: Larvae are bilaterally symmetrical while adults are typically radially symmetrical
questions.option_d: Both larva and adult are always asymmetrical
questions.explanation: Echinoderms are typically pentaradial as adults, while their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A marine animal has a notochord at least during embryonic development and a post-anal tail at some stage. Which broader group includes it?
questions.explanation: A notochord and post-anal tail, together with other diagnostic characters, are characteristic of chordates at some stage of development.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A survey finds a hollow nerve cord running along the dorsal side of an embryo. This arrangement is characteristic of which group?
questions.explanation: Chordates have a dorsal hollow nerve cord; many invertebrate groups instead have ventral solid nerve cords or nerve nets.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An insect hatches as a nymph resembling a small adult and develops without a pupal stage. Which type of metamorphosis does it undergo?
questions.explanation: In incomplete metamorphosis, the young nymph resembles a smaller adult and develops through moults without a pupal stage.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A vertebrate-like marine animal has a notochord and dorsal nerve cord only during its larval stage; the adult is attached and filter-feeding. Which group is likely?
questions.explanation: In urochordates such as tunicates, the larva shows chordate features that are reduced or lost in the sessile adult.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fish skeleton is made mainly of cartilage and its gill slits are not covered by an operculum. Which class is indicated?
questions.explanation: Cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) have a cartilaginous skeleton and typically exposed gill slits rather than a bony operculum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A reptile embryo develops within an amniotic egg with protective extraembryonic membranes. What evolutionary advantage does this provide over a jelly-coated amphibian egg?
questions.option_a: The embryo can obtain oxygen only from soil
questions.option_b: The embryo no longer needs nutrients
questions.option_c: Development can occur on land without a free-standing aquatic environment
questions.option_d: The egg prevents all water loss
questions.explanation: The amniotic egg and its membranes protect the embryo and support development on land, reducing dependence on open water for reproduction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A mammal gives birth to poorly developed young that complete much of their development in a pouch. Which group best fits?
questions.explanation: Marsupials give birth to relatively immature young that continue development attached to a teat, often in a pouch.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which mammal group lays eggs rather than giving birth to live young?
questions.explanation: Monotremes, including the platypus and echidnas, are egg-laying mammals.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A bird’s forelimbs are modified into wings, but the hindlimbs still support walking or perching. Which statement is correct?
questions.option_a: Birds have six pairs of limbs
questions.option_b: Forelimbs and hindlimbs are homologous appendages modified for different functions
questions.explanation: Bird wings are modified forelimbs; the hindlimbs serve other functions such as locomotion and perching.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A comparison finds that a whale has hair and mammary glands despite living entirely in water. Which classification criterion is strongest?
questions.option_a: Mammary glands and other mammalian traits, not habitat alone
questions.option_b: A streamlined body means it is an arthropod
questions.option_c: Absence of visible legs means it is a mollusc
questions.option_d: Aquatic habitat means it must be a fish
questions.explanation: Whales are mammals; classification relies on shared structural and developmental traits rather than simply the habitat occupied.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An arthropod cannot expand its rigid external skeleton continuously as it grows. Which process allows it to increase in size?
questions.explanation: Arthropods periodically shed the old exoskeleton by ecdysis so a larger one can form as the animal grows.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A myriapod has one pair of legs on most trunk segments. Which group does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Centipedes typically have one pair of legs per trunk segment; millipedes usually have two pairs on most apparent segments.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
